pr_title: sql,streamingest: introduce ALTER TENANT ... PAUSE/RESUME REPLICATION
pr_body:
This change introduces:
`ALTER TENANT <name> RESUME REPLICATION`
`ALTER TENANT <name> PAUSE REPLICATION`

These statements can be used to pause and resume the replication job if the tenant is being replicated into.

Fixes: #91246

Release note: None

issue_context.title: c2c: introduce `ALTER TENANT` grammar
issue_context.body:
Once we start persisting the job ID of the ingestion job in the tenant record as part of #91240, flavours of `ALTER TENANT` will be our primary interface to interact with the streaming job. This issue tracks two of the quickest wins around pausing and resuming the streaming job.

- [ ] `ALTER TENANT <name> PAUSE REPLICATION`
- [ ] `ALTER TENANT <name> RESUME REPLICATION`

Jira issue: CRDB-21174

Epic CRDB-18749

review_comments:
> {`ALTER TENANT ALL ??`, `ALTER TENANT CLUSTER SETTING`},
		{`ALTER TENANT ALL SET ??`, `ALTER TENANT CLUSTER SETTING`},
		{`ALTER TENANT ALL RESET ??`, `ALTER TENANT CLUSTER SETTING`},
		{`ALTER TENANT 'foo' RESUME REPLICATION ??`, `ALTER TENANT REPLICATION`},
		{`ALTER TENANT 'foo' PAUSE REPLICATION ??`, `ALTER TENANT REPLICATION`},

shouldn't the keys on the right be ALTER TENANT?

I believe the way to read this test is the more tokens you type on the left the more specific help text you get, atleast thats my understanding 😅 . So an `ALTER TENANT ALL ??` is currently only supported for altering a tenant cluster setting and so that's the help text we see.

`GetTenantRecordByName()` doesn't do a system tenant check or an admin check.  We might want to add those above here so that we get a good error message.

We should probably clean up how some of this is factored in a follow-up PR.
good point, added a system tenant check, admin privilege check as well as an enterprise check.

This is a general issue with a number of our Opaque statements at the moment, but I _think_ that this statement will still be allowed during read-only transactions.  One option would be to update CanWriteData in this same file.
nice catch, added `CanWriteData` and a test.
